subject: physics
title: Moments, couples and equilibrium
key_idea: The moment of a force is the force times the perpendicular distance from the pivot. A body is in equilibrium when there is no resultant force and no resultant moment, so the clockwise moments equal the anticlockwise moments about any point.

sections.heading: Moment of a force and centre of gravity

blocks.text: A force can turn an object about a point. This section covers the moment of a force and where the weight of an object acts.

items.meaning: The force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
The straight line along which a force acts.
The single point through which the whole weight of an object may be taken to act.
The point at which the whole mass of an object may be taken to be concentrated.

blocks.label: Moment of a force
where: moment = turning effect about the pivot (N m)
x = perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force (m)

items: A moment is clockwise or anticlockwise about a chosen point.
The distance must be measured at right angles to the force. If the force is at an angle θ to the rod, the perpendicular distance is d sin θ.
A longer spanner gives a greater moment for the same force.
The centre of gravity of a uniform regular solid is at its centre. In a uniform gravitational field it is at the same point as the centre of mass.
The weight of an object can be drawn as one force acting at its centre of gravity.

blocks.text: Finding the centre of gravity experimentally

items.text: Hang an irregular flat card from a pin so it swings freely.
Hang a plumb line from the pin. Mark where it crosses the card.
Hang the card from two more holes and mark each line.
The lines cross at the centre of gravity. The card balances on a pin placed there.

items: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.
The weight of an object acts through its centre of gravity.
A hanging object comes to rest with its centre of gravity vertically below the pivot.

blocks.text: Some forces turn an object without moving it as a whole. This section covers the couple.

items.meaning: A pair of equal and opposite coplanar forces whose lines of action do not coincide. It produces rotation only.
One of the forces multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the lines of action of the forces.

blocks.label: Torque of a couple
where: torque = turning effect of the couple (N m)
F = size of one of the forces (N)
d = perpendicular distance between the lines of action of the forces (m)

items: The two forces are equal and opposite, so the resultant force is zero. The object does not accelerate in a straight line.
The forces do not act along the same line, so they have a resultant torque and cause rotation only.
Examples are turning a steering wheel with two hands, a tap or a key.
The torque of a couple is the same about any point, because the total moment of the two forces is the same about every point.
A couple is two equal, opposite, parallel forces. It gives rotation without translation.
Torque of a couple = one force × the perpendicular distance between the forces.

sections.heading: The principle of moments and equilibrium

blocks.text: An object that is not accelerating and not turning is in equilibrium. This section covers the conditions for this.

items.meaning: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about that point.
There is no resultant force and no resultant torque on the body.

items: Forces in equilibrium: the resultant force is zero, so there is no linear acceleration.
Moments in equilibrium: the resultant moment is zero about any point, so there is no angular acceleration.
Choose a pivot where an unknown force acts. That force then has no moment about it, which removes it from the equation.

items.text: A uniform 2.0 m plank of weight 40 N is pivoted at its centre. A 60 N child sits 0.80 m to the left of the pivot. How far to the right must an 80 N adult sit?

diagram.alt: A practice calculation. Use the principle of moments to find a distance on a balanced beam.
diagram.question: A beam is balanced on a pivot. A {F1} N weight hangs {d1} m to the left of the pivot. A {F2} N weight hangs on the right. How far from the pivot must it hang? Ignore the weight of the beam.

items: Three coplanar forces are in equilibrium if their resultant is zero and their lines of action pass through one point.
Drawn tip to tail, the three vectors form a closed triangle, called the triangle of forces.
The triangle can be drawn to scale, or the sides found using trigonometry.
If the triangle does not close, there is a resultant force.
Equilibrium needs zero resultant force and zero resultant moment.
Principle of moments: clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments about any point.
Three forces in equilibrium make a closed vector triangle.

checks.a: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.

checks.q: Two forces of 15 N, equal and opposite, act on a wheel at opposite ends of a diameter of 0.40 m. Calculate the torque of the couple.
State the two conditions for a body to be in equilibrium.
checks.a: The resultant force on it is zero, and the resultant torque (moment) about any point is zero.
